evidence_chain: Fact: NewMarket announced that its board approved up to $100 million of capital investment by AMPAC to expand ammonium perchlorate production capabilities in support of growing solid rocket motor demand; the project would add an additional production line, increase capacity by more than 50%, and was scheduled for completion during 2026. Source: https://www.newmarket.com/news/2025/04/newmarket-corporation-announces-approval-of-ampac-expansion/

Fact: AMPAC separately described itself as a leading supplier of critical materials for solid rocket propulsion and said the expansion at the Cedar City, Utah facility was a response to demand from U.S. and allied defense programs and civil space launch systems. Source: https://www.ampac.us/press-release-100-million-capacity-expansion/

Fact: AMPAC’s product page states that it is a worldwide leader in ammonium perchlorate and that AP is primarily used as a key component in solid rocket propellant across aerospace, national defense, commercial, and space sectors. Source: https://www.ampac.us/perchlorates
Fact: AMPAC’s website states that American Pacific is the North American manufacturer of ammonium perchlorate. Source: https://www.ampac.us/what-we-do/

Fact: NewMarket’s Q3 2025 release stated that specialty materials sales were $38.2 million in Q3 2025 versus $59.1 million in Q3 2024, and that 2024 specialty materials results reflect AMPAC only since the January 16, 2024 acquisition. Source: https://www.newmarket.com/news/2025/10/newmarket-corporation-reports-third-quarter-and-first-nine-months-2025-results/

Fact: NewMarket’s Q3 2025 release also stated that, through AMPAC and Calca acquisitions and capacity investments, the company had committed approximately $1 billion to its specialty materials segment. Source: https://www.newmarket.com/news/2025/10/newmarket-corporation-reports-third-quarter-and-first-nine-months-2025-results/

Fact: CNAS argued in May 2026 that the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile, and that subtier suppliers can be vulnerable to uneven demand signals and appropriations. Source: https://www.cnas.org/publications/commentary/new-dib-rue

Inference: If AMPAC is indeed a scarce North American AP producer and AP is necessary for SRM propellant, then U.S. missile replenishment and SRM expansion could transmit demand to AMPAC even though NEU is not a defense prime.

Hypothesis: The over-50% capacity expansion may indicate pre-existing or anticipated customer demand strong enough to justify dedicated capex; however, the available evidence does not yet prove pricing power, contract structure, or NEU-level earnings sensitivity.

Speculation: If AP supply is a bottleneck and AMPAC has favorable long-term contracts, NEU could eventually be re-rated by some investors as a partial defense-industrial-base supplier rather than only as a petroleum-additives company. This requires more evidence before promotion.
falsification_plan: Check NEU 2025 10-K and subsequent 10-Q segment tables. Falsify or downgrade if specialty materials revenue, operating profit, assets, or capex remain immaterial and management does not show a credible path to materiality.
Track whether the AP expansion is completed during 2026 as disclosed. Downgrade if completion slips materially without customer-backed justification.

Look for evidence of customer-backed economics: long-term supply agreements, take-or-pay structures, prepayments, pricing escalators, cost pass-throughs, or government funding. Downgrade if expansion appears purely speculative or low-return.

Search DoD awards, DPA Title III / industrial-base funding documents, and missile-program procurement materials for AMPAC, ammonium perchlorate, perchlorate, solid rocket motor inputs, or Cedar City. Downgrade if no direct or indirect funding / demand linkage emerges.

Compare L3Harris/Aerojet, Northrop Grumman, Lockheed Martin, RTX/Raytheon, and other SRM/missile program commentary for mentions of AP or energetic-material constraints. Downgrade if bottlenecks are elsewhere and AP is not constrained.
Review environmental, safety, and permitting records for AMPAC’s Cedar City facility. Downgrade if compliance liabilities or permitting constraints make expansion economics unattractive.
Examine NEU management commentary. Downgrade if management frames AMPAC as a small adjacency with limited profit contribution rather than a scalable specialty-materials platform.
Monitor segment margins after capacity comes online. Falsify the earnings-leverage thesis if incremental specialty-materials sales do not translate into operating-profit growth.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AMPAC’s ammonium perchlorate exposure is large enough to move NEU-level economics. The strongest upgrade signal would be evidence that specialty materials, AMPAC, or AP expansion contributes meaningful consolidated revenue growth, operating income, backlog-like visibility, pricing power, take-or-pay contracts, customer prepayments, government industrial-base funding, or unusually high returns on the up-to-$100 million expansion capex. The strongest downgrade signal would be that AMPAC remains too small, low-margin, cost-heavy, environmentally constrained, or contractually capped to matter at the parent-company level.
next_research_tasks: Pull NEU’s latest 10-K and 10-Q filings and build a table for petroleum additives versus specialty materials: revenue, operating profit, operating margin, assets, depreciation, capex, and working capital.

Quantify the up-to-$100 million AMPAC expansion relative to NEU consolidated capex, operating cash flow, EBITDA, and specialty-materials sales to assess whether management is making a company-level capital-allocation bet.

Search SEC filings for the acquisition accounting of AMPAC: purchase price, goodwill, identifiable intangible assets, customer relationships, useful lives, and any earnout or contingent consideration.

Search DoD contract awards, USASpending, DPA Title III announcements, Army/Navy/Air Force industrial-base documents, and missile-production budget justifications for AMPAC, American Pacific, ammonium perchlorate, perchlorate, and Cedar City.

Map downstream demand by program: PAC-3, THAAD, GMLRS, AMRAAM, Standard Missile, hypersonics, strategic missiles, and space launch boosters; then determine which programs use AP-based SRMs and which integrators buy from AMPAC directly or indirectly.

Interview-style research question for future filings/calls: ask whether the AP expansion is supported by firm customer commitments, cost-plus arrangements, long-term supply agreements, or government-backed funding.
Review EPA, Utah environmental, OSHA, ATF, DOT hazardous-material, and local permitting records for AMPAC’s Cedar City operations to understand expansion constraints and liability profile.
Benchmark AMPAC against other energetic-material suppliers and SRM bottleneck names to determine whether AP is a true chokepoint or just one of several constrained inputs.
Track NEU’s future specialty-materials disclosures after Calca integration to separate hydrazine/propellant exposure from AMPAC/AP exposure.
Create a monitoring trigger list: AP expansion completion, specialty-materials margin inflection, new defense-space customer language, DoD funding linkage, and any customer concentration disclosure.
risks: Materiality risk: AMPAC or the specialty materials segment may be too small relative to NEU’s legacy petroleum-additives operations to materially change consolidated earnings or free cash flow.

Margin and pricing risk: Higher AP volume does not necessarily mean higher returns if contracts are cost-plus, fixed-price with limited escalators, or burdened by input, labor, safety, environmental, or compliance costs.
Capex execution risk: The up-to-$100 million AP expansion may face delays, permitting issues, cost overruns, qualification delays, commissioning risk, or lower-than-expected utilization.
Demand timing risk: Missile replenishment and SRM expansion are politics- and budget-dependent; appropriations delays or program reprioritization could weaken order timing.
Customer concentration risk: A narrow set of defense, space, or SRM customers could create negotiating leverage against AMPAC or introduce volatility if a program changes.
Regulatory and environmental risk: Perchlorates and energetic materials can carry safety, environmental, transportation, and remediation liabilities that may offset demand upside.

Substitution / supply response risk: The thesis weakens if alternative qualified supply can enter quickly, if customers dual-source more effectively than expected, or if integrators internalize or bypass AMPAC.
Disclosure risk: NEU may not provide enough granular AMPAC-level data for outside investors to confidently model revenue, margins, backlog, or customer economics.
Valuation risk: Even if the hidden exposure is real, the market may already capitalize it partly through NEU’s broader specialty-materials expansion or defense-adjacent acquisition narrative.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Politics / defense budget and allied replenishment demand -> missile and space launch programs -> solid rocket motor integrators such as prime/subprime missile propulsion suppliers -> solid propellant formulation -> oxidizer input ammonium perchlorate -> AMPAC production facility / NEU specialty materials segment. AMPAC is not the missile prime or SRM integrator; it appears to sit one layer upstream as a critical-material supplier for SRM propellant.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：NEU 的主要市场标签仍是石油添加剂与特种化学品，但其子公司 American Pacific Corporation（AMPAC）可能是美国固体火箭发动机产业链中 ammonium perchlorate（AP，高氯酸铵）这一关键氧化剂的稀缺供应节点。若美国导弹补库、盟友军援、太空发射和固体火箭发动机扩产继续受政治预算、国防工业基础政策和供应链韧性驱动，AMPAC 的 AP 产能扩张可能给 NEU 带来被传统化工覆盖低估的国防工业链敞口。当前结论仍应定为“有较强公开证据支持的假设”，而不是已验证的公司级盈利拐点，因为还需要确认 AMPAC / specialty materials 在 NEU 合并收入、营业利润、资本开支、客户集中度和定价权中的实际权重。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: NEU is still primarily categorized as a petroleum-additives and specialty-chemicals company, but its American Pacific Corporation subsidiary may sit on a scarce U.S. solid-rocket-motor input node: ammonium perchlorate, the oxidizer used in solid rocket propellant. If U.S. missile replenishment, allied defense demand, civil space launch, and SRM capacity expansion remain policy- and budget-driven priorities, AMPAC’s AP capacity expansion could create a hidden defense-industrial-base exposure that conventional chemicals coverage may under-model. The thesis should be treated as a publicly supported hypothesis, not a proven NEU-level earnings inflection, until segment materiality, margins, capex, customer concentration, and pricing power are verified.

Chemicals investors may focus on lubricant and fuel additives, volumes, margins, and general industrial cycles rather than on missile replenishment, SRM bottlenecks, Defense Production Act logic, environmental permitting, qualification cycles, or single-source / low-source defense inputs. This creates a possible classification mismatch: the hidden asset may be more relevant to the defense industrial base than NEU’s top-level industry label implies.

deep_reports.company: Karman Holdings Inc. / Karman Space & Defense
evidence_chain: Fact: Karman’s Q1 2026 10-Q states that the company specializes in mission-critical system solutions for launch vehicle, satellite, spacecraft, missile defense, hypersonic, and UAS customers, with payload protection, propulsion, and hydro/aerodynamic interstage systems deployed across priority Department of War and space initiatives. Source: SEC 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040127/000119312526222116/krmn-20260331.htm

Fact: Karman’s Q1 2026 10-Q states it delivers payload protection, propulsion and launch, and hydro/aerodynamic interstage systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting more than 130 space and defense programs. Source: SEC 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040127/000119312526222116/krmn-20260331.htm

Fact: Karman reported Q1 2026 revenue of $151.210M versus $100.124M in Q1 2025, a 51.0% increase, and backlog of $1.026903B versus $636.350M. Source: SEC 10-Q lines on KPIs/backlog, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040127/000119312526222116/krmn-20260331.htm

Fact: Karman’s Q1 2026 revenue by end market included Hypersonics and Strategic Missile Defense of $35.688M, Space and Launch of $43.854M, Tactical Missiles and Integrated Defense Systems of $45.260M, and Maritime Defense Systems of $26.408M. Source: SEC 10-Q revenue disaggregation, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040127/000119312526222116/krmn-20260331.htm

Fact: Karman stated that Tactical Missiles and Integrated Defense Systems growth in Q1 2026 was driven by demand related to advanced drone and loitering munitions technologies and increased production output for GMLRS. Source: SEC 10-Q MD&A, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040127/000119312526222116/krmn-20260331.htm

Fact: Karman announced that its Systima facility in Mukilteo, Washington received $5.0M in Defense Production Act Title III funding to expand capacity to produce solid rocket motor nozzles. Source: BusinessWire/StockTitan republication, https://www.stocktitan.net/news/KRMN/pentagon-awards-systima-part-of-karman-space-defense-5-million-to-lhumgezf88hu.html

Fact: The same announcement says the award supports munitions-industrial-base objectives, supply-chain resiliency, domestic production in strategic priority areas, and increasing capacity across key nodes of the SRM component supply chain. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/KRMN/pentagon-awards-systima-part-of-karman-space-defense-5-million-to-lhumgezf88hu.html

Fact: Karman stated it has designed, produced, and delivered SRM nozzles in support of key missile programs for several decades and intends to create an additional dedicated SRM nozzle production line for a major production program plus an optimized production cell for complex nozzles. Source: https://www.stocktitan.net/news/KRMN/pentagon-awards-systima-part-of-karman-space-defense-5-million-to-lhumgezf88hu.html

Fact: Karman’s 2025 annual-report materials disclose acquisitions of MTI, ISP, Five Axis, and Seemann/Materials Sciences, with ISP expanding small-diameter solid propellant and energetic propulsion systems, and MTI expanding advanced materials for strategic missile defense. Source: SEC annual report PDF, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2040127/000114036126013924/edge20063633x772_ars.pdf

Context fact: CNAS argued in May 2026 that the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile, and that subtier suppliers remain exposed to uneven demand signals and appropriations. Source: CNAS, https://www.cnas.org/publications/commentary/new-dib-rue

Context fact: External search context reports L3Harris received a $1B government investment to accelerate solid rocket motor capacity expansion and functions as a first-tier SRM supplier to Lockheed Martin and Raytheon on programs such as PAC-3 and THAAD. Source from provided search context: https://www.druckfin.com/en/articles/l3harris-fires-on-all-cylinders-15-organic-growth-40b-backlog-and-a-missile-unit-20260430

Inference: Karman’s DPA-funded SRM nozzle expansion, missile/hypersonics revenue growth, and large backlog together support a plausible chokepoint thesis, but they do not by themselves prove SRM-nozzle revenue materiality or multi-prime qualification.

Hypothesis: if SRM nozzles require long qualification cycles, specialized ablative/high-temperature manufacturing, and program-specific production cells, Karman may have more pricing power and revenue elasticity than a generic aerospace-components label implies.
falsification_plan: Falsify if Karman’s next filings or calls show SRM nozzle revenue is immaterial within total revenue or not separable from broader propulsion/launch systems.
Falsify if the DPA-funded nozzle line is one-off, small, or tied to a single low-volume program rather than repeated production demand.
Falsify if backlog growth is mainly from Space and Launch, Maritime Defense Systems, or acquired businesses rather than missile/SRM/hypersonics programs.
Falsify if management avoids or contradicts claims of multi-program SRM nozzle exposure, or if no evidence emerges of qualification with major SRM/missile ecosystems.
Falsify if gross margin or adjusted EBITDA margin deteriorates during the capacity ramp, indicating the bottleneck lacks pricing power or has poor manufacturing yields.
Falsify if primes/SRM leaders announce internal nozzle capacity or alternate qualified suppliers that reduce dependence on Karman/Systima.
Falsify if DPA/DoD industrial-base awards for SRM nozzles flow primarily to other suppliers while Karman receives no follow-on support or orders.
Falsify if Q2-Q4 2026 revenue growth decelerates materially despite strong backlog, suggesting conversion, execution, or demand-timing issues.
deep_reports.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the DPA-funded Systima nozzle expansion is tied to one major production program or multiple missile/SRM programs; whether SRM nozzle revenue is material inside Karman’s Propulsion & Launch Systems and missile/hypersonics revenue; whether Karman is qualified across L3Harris/Aerojet, Northrop Grumman, RTX/Raytheon, Lockheed Martin, or newer SRM/munition entrants; and whether backlog growth is directly linked to SRM/missile capacity rather than broader space, maritime, or acquisition-driven revenue.
next_research_tasks: Read Karman’s full S-1, FY2025 10-K/annual report, Q1 2026 10-Q, and May/June 2026 prospectus filings to extract segment/end-market mix, backlog definition, customer concentration, controlled-company/secondary-offering dynamics, and acquisition-adjusted organic growth.

Build a product-to-program matrix: SRM nozzles, propulsion systems, energetic propulsion, payload protection, interstage systems, advanced materials, Seemann composites, MTI advanced materials, ISP small-diameter solid propulsion, Five Axis liquid propulsion engine nozzles.

Search DoD, DPA Title III, SAM.gov, FPDS/USAspending, and DoD contract announcements for Systima, Karman, SRM nozzles, nozzle cells, ablative components, GMLRS, PAC-3, THAAD, AMRAAM, PrSM, hypersonics, and munitions-industrial-base awards.
Check whether the $5.0M DPA award has a public project description, period of performance, cost share, production-capacity target, program name, and follow-on award potential.

Review L3Harris/Aerojet, Northrop Grumman, RTX/Raytheon, and Lockheed Martin transcripts for mentions of SRM nozzles, ablatives, qualified suppliers, supplier bottlenecks, munitions acceleration, GMLRS, PAC-3, THAAD, AMRAAM, PrSM, and hypersonics.

Ask management or IR directly: what percentage of revenue/backlog is propulsion, what percentage is SRM nozzle-related, how many missile programs use Karman nozzles, and what is the qualification timeline for a new nozzle supplier.

Track quarterly KPIs: backlog, book-to-bill if disclosed, revenue by end market, gross margin, adjusted EBITDA margin, capex, inventory, contract assets/liabilities, customer concentration, and acquisition-adjusted organic growth.

Compare with reference leaders and shadow suppliers: L3Harris/Aerojet as SRM reference leader; Northrop, RTX, and Lockheed as demand-channel references; smaller subtier suppliers such as connectors, inspection, energetic materials, ablatives, tooling, and test providers as alternative chokepoints.
Separate politics-driven demand from company execution: map NDAA/appropriations/DPA awards to actual purchase orders and backlog conversion rather than assuming policy headlines equal revenue.

Create an evidence-upgrade ladder: Level 1 equals DPA award only; Level 2 equals disclosed SRM nozzle backlog/orders; Level 3 equals multi-program, multi-prime qualification evidence; Level 4 equals margin-accretive revenue conversion; Level 5 equals repeat follow-on awards plus sustained backlog and pricing/operating leverage.
risks: Evidence gap risk: public disclosures confirm SRM nozzle capacity expansion but do not yet quantify SRM nozzle revenue, margin, backlog, program count, or customer mix.
Program concentration risk: the DPA announcement references a major production program; if this is one narrow program rather than multiple missile families, the chokepoint thesis is weaker.
Customer substitution risk: primes or SRM producers may dual-source, vertically integrate, or qualify alternate nozzle suppliers faster than assumed.
Acquisition complexity risk: Karman’s growth includes acquisitions such as MTI, ISP, Five Axis, and Seemann/Materials Sciences; integration may obscure organic missile/SRM growth or pressure margins.
Policy and appropriations risk: missile and munitions demand is politically driven; budget delays, changing priorities, export restrictions, or procurement changes can affect timing.
Capacity-ramp risk: DPA funding and internal capex may add cost before revenue, and production cells may face labor, materials, yield, certification, or schedule constraints.

Valuation/attention risk: after the IPO and rising public visibility, part of the defense/space growth story may already be priced; this report does not provide a buy/sell recommendation or price target.
Disclosure risk: classified or sensitive programs may limit investor visibility, making it difficult to verify customer qualification and program breadth.
Margin risk: cost of goods sold rose with materials and labor in Q1 2026; operating leverage must continue to offset ramp costs.
Float/secondary-offering risk: recent secondary-offering and lockup dynamics can affect market technicals independent of the industrial thesis.
deep_reports.supply_chain_position: Politics/policy driver -> U.S. and allied missile replenishment, munitions capacity, hypersonics, strategic missile defense, GMLRS/drone/loitering-munition adoption -> missile primes and SRM producers such as Lockheed Martin, RTX/Raytheon, Northrop Grumman, and L3Harris/Aerojet Rocketdyne as reference leaders -> subtier propulsion and high-temperature components -> Karman/Systima as a potential SRM nozzle, propulsion-and-launch systems, payload protection, hydro/aerodynamic interstage, energetic propulsion, and advanced-materials supplier. Fact: Karman says it delivers payload protection, propulsion, and interstage systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting more than 130 space and defense programs. Inference: if SRM nozzles are qualified, multi-program, and hard to substitute, this subtier node could capture operating leverage from policy-driven munitions capacity expansion.
deep_reports.thesis_cn: 假设：Karman 可能不是普通航天/国防零部件公司，而是更接近美国导弹补库存、固体火箭发动机产能扩张、耐烧蚀/高温结构件和推进系统组件的公开市场映射。已验证事实包括：公司披露其服务发射器、卫星、航天器、导弹防御、高超音速和 UAS 客户；2026 年一季度收入同比增长 51.0%，backlog 达约 10.27 亿美元；其 Systima 工厂获得 500 万美元 Defense Production Act Title III 资金，用于扩大固体火箭发动机喷管产能。关键未证实部分是：SRM 喷管收入占比、项目数量、客户认证深度、是否服务多个主要导弹项目，以及客户是否难以绕开或快速双源。
deep_reports.thesis_en: Hypothesis: Karman may be more than a generic aerospace-and-defense component company. It may be a relatively pure public-market mapping to U.S. missile replenishment, solid rocket motor capacity expansion, ablative/high-temperature structures, and propulsion-adjacent components. Verified public evidence shows that Karman serves launch vehicle, satellite, spacecraft, missile defense, hypersonic, and UAS customers; Q1 2026 revenue rose 51.0% year over year and backlog reached about $1.027B; and its Systima facility received a $5.0M Defense Production Act Title III award to expand solid rocket motor nozzle production capacity. The unresolved proof points are SRM-nozzle revenue materiality, breadth across missile programs, depth of qualification with primes/SRM players, and whether customers can bypass or dual-source the function quickly.

deep_reports.why_underfollowed: Karman is no longer invisible after its IPO and secondary offering activity, but the market may still label it broadly as space, hypersonics, missile defense, or aerospace components. The hidden research angle is narrower: whether Karman owns qualified SRM nozzle capacity and high-temperature propulsion-adjacent manufacturing know-how that are hard to replicate on political/appropriations time scales. This can be missed because subtier suppliers are often buried below primes, because program names may not be fully disclosed, and because broad end-market revenue categories do not isolate SRM nozzle economics.

Downgrade the thesis if customers have many qualified alternative ablative-material suppliers with short switching timelines.

risks: [Evidence gap] Public evidence does not yet prove the exact missile programs, prime customers, qualification status, or single-source role for PKE's ablative/nozzle materials.
[Materiality risk] Rocket-nozzle or C2B/RAYCARB-related sales may still be too small relative to total revenue to drive consolidated earnings.
[Substitution risk] Even if PKE supplies relevant materials, customers may have multiple qualified suppliers or the ability to dual-source over time.
[Supplier-dependence risk] If RAYCARB supply from ArianeGroup is itself constrained, PKE may face availability risk rather than pricing power.
[Customer concentration/program timing risk] Defense and space orders can be lumpy, delayed by appropriations, qualification cycles, export controls, or prime-contractor scheduling.
[Commercial aerospace dilution] PKE's commercial aerospace and general composite-structures exposure may dominate results, weakening the missile-rearmament thesis.
[Margin risk] Specialty material revenue growth does not automatically mean higher margins if input costs, qualification costs, inventory, tariffs, or working-capital needs rise.
[Market-pricing risk] The market may already price some aerospace/defense recovery into PKE despite low thematic attention.

deep_reports.thesis_cn: PKE 的主流标签是航空航天复合材料，而不是导弹或弹药产能扩张标的。但其公开 10-K 和公司材料显示，公司提供用于火箭发动机和喷管的特种耐烧蚀材料，并且是 ArianeGroup RAYCARB C2B NG 在北美的独家分销商；该材料被描述为用于生产关键火箭和导弹系统的耐烧蚀复合材料。因此，若美国及盟友导弹补库、PAC-3/THAAD/AMRAAM 等相关固体火箭发动机扩产继续推动上游耐烧蚀材料需求，PKE 可能位于一个较隐蔽的二级/三级供应链节点。真正需要验证的是：这些材料是否进入受限推进系统、是否经过严格认证、是否难以替代，以及火箭喷管/耐烧蚀材料收入是否足以影响公司收入和毛利。
deep_reports.thesis_en: [Hypothesis, partially fact-supported] PKE is usually screened as an aerospace-composites company rather than as a missile-capacity or munitions-ramp supplier. However, its public filings and company materials state that Park offers specialty ablative materials for rocket motors and nozzles, and that it is the exclusive North American distributor for ArianeGroup's RAYCARB C2B NG product, described as an input for ablative composite materials used in critical rocketry and missile systems. If U.S./allied missile replenishment and solid-rocket-motor capacity expansion continue, PKE may sit in a hidden subtier node tied to high-temperature ablatives/nozzle materials. The key unresolved proof is whether these materials are qualified into constrained propulsion applications, hard to substitute, and large enough to create meaningful revenue or margin sensitivity.
